Here's what I found tracing the zero-coordinate path through the code.

**The write gate (when `log_void=0`):**
- [sd_logger.cpp:129](bgeigiezen_firmware/handlers/sd_logger.cpp#L129) writes only when `LogAggregator::valid()` is true.
- [log_aggregator.h:16-18](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/log_aggregator.h#L16-L18): `valid() = gps_valid && gm_valid && dop_valid`.
- `gps_valid` ← `gps_data.valid()` ← `location_valid && date_valid && time_valid` (h:32-34).

**Where zeroes enter the LOG line:**
[log_aggregator.cpp:62-94](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/log_aggregator.cpp#L62-L94) initializes `latitude_dm = latitude_s = longitude_dm = longitude_s = 0` and only fills them inside `if (gps_data.valid())`. So a zero-coord line is only emitted when `gps_data.valid() == false` at line 69.

**The bug — TOCTOU on the gps_data reference.** `gps_data` is a `const auto&` reference (line 53), and `.valid()` is read three separate times in this function:

1. Line 69 — gates the lat/lon formatting.
2. Line 97 — `gps_valid` for the log-line `'A'/'V'` flag and `dop_valid`.
3. Line 123 — `data.gps_valid`, which feeds `LogAggregator::valid()` and thus the SdLogger gate.

If `gps_data.valid()` flips **false → true** between line 69 and line 123, you get exactly the symptom: lat_dm/lon_dm stay zero (line 69 path skipped), but `data.gps_valid = true` (line 123) lets sd_logger write the line. The flip is plausible because [gps_connector.cpp:814](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/gps_connector.cpp#L814) clears `location_valid` on timer expiry, then the next NAV-PVT frame restores it; if another worker preempts mid-function, the reads diverge.

The OP's hypothesis (tighten `fixType` to 3-only at [gps_connector.cpp:735](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/gps_connector.cpp#L735)) doesn't explain the symptom — a 2D fix has valid lat/lon, just a synthetic altitude=0 ([:767](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/gps_connector.cpp#L767)). It would just reject more good fixes.

**Minimal patch (not yet applied — want your sign-off first):** snapshot validity and coordinates once at the top of `LogAggregator::produce_data()` and use the snapshot everywhere:

```cpp
const auto& gps_data = workers.worker<GpsConnector>(k_worker_gps_connector)->get_data();
const bool gps_valid_snap = gps_data.valid();
const double lat_snap = gps_data.latitude;
const double lon_snap = gps_data.longitude;
// ...use gps_valid_snap, lat_snap, lon_snap throughout instead of re-reading
```

This eliminates the TOCTOU regardless of which worker preempts.

**Suggested reply on the issue (covering louisbertrand's questions):**

> Traced the path: `0000.0000,0000.0000` is written when `LogAggregator::valid()` evaluates true at write time but `gps_data.valid()` was false when the line was formatted. `gps_data` is held by reference and `.valid()` is re-read three times in [`log_aggregator.cpp:69, 97, 123`](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/log_aggregator.cpp#L69) — a flip false→true between calls (e.g. `location_timer` expires then a fresh NAV-PVT lands) reproduces it.
>
> The `getFixType() == 2 || 3` gate is fine: 2D fixes still carry valid lat/lon; only altitude is forced to 0 at [`gps_connector.cpp:767`](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/gps_connector.cpp#L767). Tightening to fixType==3 would drop usable fixes without addressing the zero-coord case.
>
> Suggested fix: snapshot `gps_data.valid()`, `latitude`, `longitude` once at the top of `LogAggregator::produce_data()` and use the locals throughout. Want me to push a PR?
>
> @louisbertrand — re module/firmware: this analysis is independent of the receiver model, so M7/M8/M10 should all hit it.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix: snapshot GPS state in LogAggregator to prevent zero-coord LOG lines

The gps_data reference could be mutated by GpsConnector between three
separate gps_data.valid() reads in produce_data() (lines 69, 97, 123),
letting latitude_dm/longitude_dm stay zero from the line-69 path while
data.gps_valid was still set true at line 123 — so SdLogger wrote
0000.0000,0000.0000 lines despite log_void=0.

Snapshot validity, lat/lon, altitude, pdop, sats and date/time once at
the top and use the locals throughout. Independent of receiver model
(M7 NMEA, M8/M10 UBX).

Fixes Codeberg #5.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

content.text:
Long-standing — about **2.5 years old**.

The three-read pattern over a `const auto&` reference has been there since the log aggregator was first written: commit `5a2632c9` ([Jelle Bouwhuis, 2023-11-13](https://github.com/Safecast/bGeigieZen/commit/5a2632c9)) already had `gps_data.valid()` called three times in the same shape. Subsequent commits modified surrounding logic (DOP, fixed mode, distance, etc.) but never collapsed the multiple reads.

So the latent TOCTOU has been shipping since **November 2023**. The reason it surfaces only occasionally — and only got reported now via [Codeberg #5](https://codeberg.org/Safecast/bGeigieZen/issues/5) — is that triggering it needs a narrow race: the GPS `location_timer` has to expire and a new NAV-PVT has to land *between* lines 69 and 123 of `LogAggregator::produce_data()`. That window is small enough to look "random" in field logs, which is exactly how louisbertrand described it.

input.description: Inspect GPS produce_data flow for stale-data issues

content.text:
Audit findings. Most aren't as severe as the TOCTOU we just fixed, but a few are likely contributing to the "slow lock" feel and one is a real M8/M10 status-bar bug.

**1. Same TOCTOU pattern in `DateTimeProvider`** — [rtc_connector.cpp:36-44, :59-79](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/rtc_connector.cpp#L36-L79). `gps_data` reference is checked at [:38](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/rtc_connector.cpp#L38), passed to `gps_to_system()`, re-checked at [:60](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/rtc_connector.cpp#L60), then year/month/day fields read at [:64-69](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/rtc_connector.cpp#L64-L69). Mostly safe because `GpsConnector` writes fields *before* setting `date_valid=true`, and writes `date_valid=false` *before* zeroing fields on expiry — but the safer pattern matches what we just applied to LogAggregator.

**2. `data.numSV` is never populated in UBX mode** — real M8/M10 bug. [gps_connector.cpp:733](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/gps_connector.cpp#L733) writes only `data.satsInView = _gnss.getNumSV()`. The status-bar logic at [gfx_screen.cpp:411-422](bgeigiezen_firmware/gfx_screen.cpp#L411-L422) uses `numSV>0` to decide "GPS12 orange (tracking, no fix yet)" vs "GPS? (searching)". On M8/M10 `data.numSV` stays at 0, so users jump from "GPS?" straight to "GPS5 green" with no intermediate feedback — feels like the device hangs and then suddenly locks. NMEA path sets `data.numSV` correctly from GPGSV at [:1084](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/gps_connector.cpp#L1084).

**3. First valid UBX fix is silently dropped** — [gps_connector.cpp:768, :782](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/gps_connector.cpp#L768-L782). The distance-sanity gate `distance_step < 0.5 km` rejects the first fix because `_last_latitude=_last_longitude=0`, making `haversine(real, (0,0)) ≈ thousands of km`. The NMEA path has a `first_fix` bypass at [:1048, :1056](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/gps_connector.cpp#L1048-L1056); UBX is missing it. Costs ~1 second of TTFF and burns one valid sample on every cold start.

**4. `activate()` blocks for up to ~9s on a warm boot** — auto-baud sweep can take ~5s of cumulative `1200ms` waits ([:76-167](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/gps_connector.cpp#L76-L167)), and once connected `restoreDatabaseFromSD()` runs a quiet-time loop that can stretch to 8s ([:469](bgeigiezen_firmware/workers/gps_connector.cpp#L469)). This all happens on the worker's first activation, blocking the main loop. Splitting warm-seed/DBD-restore into a non-blocking first-iteration path (or running it after the first fix instead of before) would let the UI come up immediately.

**5. Auto-baud sweep is sequential** — 4 rates × 1.2s = ~5s in the worst case. Could shorten by sniffing UART bytes first to pick a baud, or by raising the per-rate gate timeout. Not a correctness issue.

**Smallest-blast-radius wins, in order I'd recommend tackling:**
1. Fix #2 (`data.numSV` in UBX) — one line, immediately improves user perception of TTFF on M8/M10.
2. Fix #3 (UBX first-fix bypass) — port the NMEA `first_fix` pattern to the UBX path.
3. Apply the snapshot pattern to `DateTimeProvider` (#1) — defensive hardening matching the fix we just shipped.
4. Refactor `activate()` blocking I/O (#4) — bigger change, weigh against current behaviour.

Want me to go ahead with #2 and #3 as small follow-up PRs, or hold for review?

feedback while satellites were being acquired.

real coordinates produced a multi-thousand-km distance. NMEA mode had
a first_fix bypass at gps_connector.cpp:1048,1056; UBX did not. Cost
was ~1 second of TTFF and one wasted sample on every cold start.
